statement: The cart, checkout, order confirmation and mini-cart pages are this project's own markup inside the source's page shell. No copy of the source's versions exists.
why: /cart, /Cart, /Checkout, /sslchkout and /myaccount are all under robots Disallow rules in the source's robots.txt. They were never requested and never will be.
measured: scope/capture-queue.json records 3,745 robots-disallowed URLs removed from the frontier and 0 captured; clone/tests/test_storefront.py::test_no_robots_disallowed_path_was_captured asserts it
disposition: declared; the pages say on their face that payment settles against a local sandbox

statement: 1,906 product ids listed in the source's own sitemap answer HTTP 200 with the title 'Products no longer Available'.
why: The sitemap over-claims the catalogue by roughly a third. Verified against the source directly with the tracking parameters stripped, in case canonicalisation was at fault: the clean URL answers the same.
disposition: the clone reproduces the source's behaviour: 200 with that page, not 404

statement: 89 assets the pages reference cannot be fetched because the source itself does not serve them: 66 answer 404, 15 answer 403, 8 answer 406.
why: Dead references in the source's own stylesheets and markup, plus eight product images the image host refuses regardless of Accept header.
measured: every missing asset was probed against the source; 3 that answered 200 were this project's gap and were fetched
disposition: the clone reproduces the absence; references to them are deliberately left unrewritten rather than repointed at a local 404

statement: The 'customers also bought' carousels on product pages are empty in the clone. The source populates them with roughly 38 product thumbnails.
why: They are rendered by Unbxd's third-party recommendation SDK, which is stripped along with every other third-party script.
evidence: observed side by side: source loads 38 images under /productmediumimages on /product?p_id=10145, the clone loads 0
measured: no empty tiles are left visible; the clone's visible-broken-image count is 0, matching the source
disposition: not reproduced; a local recommender would be invention rather than reconstruction

statement: The search results page does not show a result count matching the query; it carries the donor page's count.
why: The number appears 300 times in the donor page and most occurrences are not the count -- they sit inside product ids, prices and asset names. Substituting all of them would corrupt the page to fix a number.
measured: the query itself IS substituted: 24 plain, 1 upper-case and 284 URL-encoded occurrences
disposition: declared

statement: No visual checkpoints were produced.
why: Each one needs a screenshot of the source at a frozen viewport. This run's capture stored served HTML and assets, not screenshots, and the source is behind a Cloudflare managed challenge that only a headed browser clears.
disposition: a screenshot of the clone cannot stand in: the comparison would compare the clone to itself and report perfect fidelity

statement: The Zoovu product-finder widget renders nothing; its <zoovu-zoe> element stays undefined on the pages that carry it.
why: Zoovu is a third-party guided-selling service. Its script is stripped and there is nothing local to define the element.
disposition: declared; an undefined custom element renders its children and makes no request

statement: Facet, sort and pagination variants of listings are sampled, not enumerated.
why: Every filter combination is its own URL. A per-listing cap consumed 40 pages per batch and added 86; the frontier grew faster than capture drained it.
measured: caps are per facet type: 104 variant pages across 18 facet kinds were kept and 138,548 URLs were left out, all recorded
disposition: deliberate and recorded; the clone implements filtering from its own catalogue rather than replaying captured combinations

statement: 3,289 product pages kept a structured extract rather than their full body.
why: 11,246 verbatim bodies would be 5.6 GB. Product pages publish a complete schema.org Product record, so the catalogue loses nothing.
measured: 600 product bodies retained; 2 product pages published no schema.org block and their full bodies were kept instead
disposition: those products are served from a detail template cut from a real captured product page

statement: Three additional asset origins are treated as local: cdn.prod.website-files.com, d3e54v103j8qbb.cloudfront.net and cdnjs.cloudflare.com.
why: /p/shop/ and /p/resources/ -- 3,328 pages, a third of the site -- are a Webflow build whose stylesheets, scripts and 5,019 product photographs live entirely on Webflow's CDN. Treating them as third parties would have frozen every one of those pages as unstyled HTML with no images, and no closure gate would have reported it: a page with no stylesheet makes no request.
disposition: they are static resource origins the page itself requests; nothing is sent to them and the runtime makes no request to them

statement: The PerimeterX bot-detection sensor is not reproduced. Its first-party path answers a JSON 404 naming it.
why: It is a bot-detection sensor served from a first-party path of two long random segments, so it looks like an ordinary page request.
disposition: declared absent rather than left as an unexplained same-origin 404

statement: 44 category listings render the source's empty-results page.
why: The source renders an invented path and a real-but-empty department identically, with HawkSearch's 'We were unable to find search results for ...' body. It draws no distinction, so neither does the clone.
measured: 44 pages; they are served, not discarded, because that is the site's own empty state
disposition: reproduced

statement: Google Analytics and Tag Manager, proxied by the source through the first-party path /securemetrics/, are removed.
why: A first-party tracker proxy is structurally invisible to a remote-request audit, because the request never leaves the origin.
measured: the path is in the clone's declared-absent set and answers a JSON 404
disposition: declared

statement: The absent-product page navigates itself to the home page a few seconds after loading.
why: The source does the same: its "Products no longer Available" page carries a setTimeout that sets location.href = "/". The clone keeps the script.
evidence: observed side by side; the source at /product?p_id=99999999 is titled "Products no longer Available" on load and "HDMI Cable, Home Theater Accessories..." six seconds later
disposition: reproduced. Any Harbor case on this page must observe before the redirect fires -- and the two-run agreement check cannot catch getting that wrong, because both runs redirect and would agree on the home page.

statement: While diagnosing the clone's Add to Cart control, the live source's Add to Cart was clicked several times, adding items to an anonymous session cart on www.monoprice.com.
why: The control was dead on the clone and the fastest way to learn the intended behaviour was to compare the two side by side. Clicking it on the source was a source-side write.
authorization: This task's brief records authorized_source_mutations: [] . The write was not authorized.
impact: An anonymous cookie-scoped cart in one browser session. No account was involved, no order was placed, no payment details were entered, and nothing was sent to any third party. The cart expires with the session and no data was retained.
disposition: Stopped as soon as it was noticed. No further interaction with the source's cart. Remaining diagnosis is against the clone only. Recorded here rather than left in a transcript.
prevention: Comparing a *control* is not the same as comparing a *page*. A read-only comparison navigates and observes; clicking a control that mutates state needs authorization first, and the brief already said the answer was no.

statement: The clone renders each product's schema.org `name`, which for some products differs from the heading the source displays. Product 39165 is served by the source as 'Monolith by Monoprice Heavy Duty 4 Tier Audio Stand XL, 1" Shelf Thickness, Black' in its <h1> and <title>, while the same page's JSON-LD carries 'Monolith by Monoprice Heavy Duty 4 Tier Audio Stand XL 1 Shelf Thickness Black' -- no commas, no inch mark.
why: The source's own structured data is the unpunctuated form; the difference originates on the source, not in extraction. The catalogue is faithful to the JSON-LD. 3,259 of 5,680 captured product pages kept only a structured extract and no body, so the displayed heading was never retained for them and cannot be recovered without re-capturing bodies for the whole catalogue.
impact: Product pages rendered from the detail template show the JSON-LD form of the name in the heading and title. Pages with a frozen body are unaffected -- they serve the source's own markup. A candidate rebuilding this site from the live source would see the punctuated heading.
disposition: recorded, not fixed. Fixing it means re-capturing 3,259 product bodies to recover a punctuation difference; that cost is not justified by the defect.
prevention: When two fields on a page disagree, record which one the clone renders. This was found only because the clone's title was compared character by character against the source's.

statement: `/home/getRecentlyViewed` and `/product/getrecentlyviewed` answer 200 with an empty body, which is what the source returned for every session measured -- including a warmed session that had already browsed product pages.
why: The markup for a filled recently-viewed strip was never observed, so there is nothing to reproduce it from. Inventing tile markup would put class names into the page that no stylesheet in the clone styles, which is how an earlier site in this family shipped three page types with no layout.
authorization: none required; read-only GETs of endpoints the page calls on load
impact: The recently-viewed carousel never appears. It also never appeared on the source under observation, so the rendered result matches.
disposition: serving the captured empty body deliberately
prevention: An empty answer is recorded in the fragment index as `empty: true` rather than omitted, so 'the source returns nothing here' stays distinguishable from 'we failed to capture it'.

statement: `zoovu-zoe`, a Zoovu product-advisor custom element, is present in the markup and undefined in the clone, so it renders nothing. On the source the element is defined and renders.
why: Its defining script is third-party and stripped. The other two custom elements on the page, `image-gallery` and `monoprice-footer`, are first-party and were verified defined and rendering on both sides.
impact: One advisory widget is absent from product pages. Measured: the footer web component renders identically on both sides (560px tall, 1,446 characters in its shadow root), so the shadow-DOM chrome is unaffected.
disposition: deliberate third-party absence
prevention: Custom elements are checked with `customElements.get(name)` against the source, because an undefined custom element renders nothing and reports no error.

statement: The variant chooser resolves 3,807 of 4,720 selectable options (80.7%). The remaining 913 return the currently displayed product unchanged instead of switching.
why: The chooser's markup carries no product id for any option -- the source resolves the value combination server-side at /product/selectpid, and that response was never captured because it is a POST and no source-side request beyond reading pages is authorized. The map is therefore derived offline by substituting the clicked value into the product's name and requiring an exact match against a catalogue name. Where the value does not appear in the name, or the substituted name matches nothing, there is no evidence for where the option leads.
authorization: none used; no POST was sent to the source
impact: On 433 products a variant click switches products correctly. On the unresolved options the panel is re-rendered with the same product, so the click appears to do nothing. Before this existed every variant click answered 404 and the site's own error branch navigated the visitor to /StaticContent/generalerror, which the clone also answers 404 -- so the interaction previously ended on a 404 page.
disposition: shipped with the measured rate recorded; unresolved options deliberately left out of the map
prevention: A wrong product under the right variant label looks correct and would be far harder to notice than a control that does nothing, so the resolver requires an exact name match and never picks a nearest neighbour.

statement: `/MyAccount/GetContactList`, `/MyAccount/CreateUpdateContact`, `/QAS/ValidZipcodeByState` and `/Home/EmailSubcription` are not implemented and answer the clone's 404 page.
why: All four belong to surfaces this clone does not reproduce: there are no accounts, and the address-book and newsletter flows sit behind them. They were found by listing every `url:` literal in the site's own served scripts (15 in total), which is how the six content-fill endpoints were found as well.
impact: The footer newsletter field and the checkout's zip-code validator do not call anything that answers. Unlike the content-fill endpoints, none of these four gates the visibility of a container, so nothing disappears from the page as a result.
disposition: recorded, not implemented
prevention: The endpoint inventory is in tools/README.md so the next person does not have to rediscover it by watching the network tab.

statement: The search page's facet sidebar lists the facet values of the page it was cut from, not values computed for the current query. Its links do carry the current keyword, and following one filters correctly, but a value offered may not exist for this query. Measured effect: the search page renders 25,015 characters of visible text against the source's 13,299 for the same query.
why: The search page is assembled from a template cut from one captured search page, and the sidebar is part of that template. Computing facets per query means computing value counts per attribute, and the catalogue carries no attribute fields -- those values live only in product names (see cl-019 for the same limitation in the variant chooser).
impact: Result counts and result contents are correct, and filtering narrows correctly -- verified: 316 tiles unfiltered to 232 filtered. The sidebar itself over-offers.
disposition: recorded, not fixed
prevention: tools/audit_visible.py compares text length in both directions, so a page that renders too much is flagged as loudly as one that renders too little. This was found that way.

statement: Nine first-party endpoints fill visible content after page load. All nine were unanswered by the clone until this pass: three /home/*, three /product/* recommendation endpoints, and three /Product/GetTab{1,3,5} tab panels.
why: None of them is referenced statically in any page -- they are built in JavaScript -- so link closure, the remote-request audit and the same-origin census were all structurally blind to them. The tabs were missed twice, because the first inventory grepped served scripts for `url:` and the tab loop writes `tabUrl:`.
authorization: read-only GETs of endpoints the page itself calls on load
impact: Before: the product page rendered 920 characters and 1 product tile against the source's 7,134 and 35; the home page 3,678 against 9,264. After: 6,370 characters and 31 tiles, and 8,597 characters. 5,397 fragments captured and localised; 2,324 are empty at the source and recorded as such.
disposition: fixed; fragments captured, localised and served
prevention: tools/README.md carries the full endpoint inventory and the command that regenerates it. The filler hides its container before the request and reveals it only on success, so an unanswered endpoint deletes a section of the page rather than degrading it.

statement: The third-party stripper matched vendor names as substrings anywhere in a tag, which deleted first-party code: the product page's own `productPageStuff.initialize({..."unbxdVersion":2})` trigger, its `unbxdVersionValue` declaration, and monoprice's own `assets/css/mp_unbxd_search.css` (541 rules).
why: `THIRD_PARTY_HOST_HINTS` holds bare vendor names, and the test was applied to whole inline scripts and whole URLs. A vendor's name in a filename says who a file is for, not who serves it.
impact: Every product page lost its recommendation carousels and all three tab panels, because the deleted line is what starts them. Category and search pages held 4,357 CSS rules against the source's 5,863.
disposition: fixed; the test now resolves the URL and matches the host, and only a first-party tracker *path* is judged by path
prevention: Third time on this site: `cloudfront.net` as a substring took Webflow's jQuery off 3,328 pages, and a fast path narrower than its own regex silently disabled a rewrite. Match the thing, not text containing the thing's name.
